full_judgment: The suit in the above noted case was instituted in 1948 for a declaration of the plaintiffs right and interest in the suit lands as korsa tenants and for confirmation of their possession therein as well as for permanent injunction responding the defendants including the Government from interfering with their possession in any madher. The suit land appertaining to the plots in suit diluviated and after reformation in situ and after it became fit for possossion the owners of the Estate settled the same with the predecessors of the plaintiffs on the basis of a korsa kabuliyat dated 1st January 1331 B.S. corresponding to May, 1924. Rents of the said newly created jamas having fallen in arrear the landlords in execution of a decree obtained by them, purchased the same in auction and settled in 1344-45 B.S. with the predecessors of some of the plaintiffs on the basis of a kabuliyat. The rent receiving interest of the landlords having been acquired under the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the Government  stepped into the shoes of the previous landlords and the plaintiffs became tenants directly under the Government but some of the lands had been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government. This led to filing of the suit. The suit was contested by the Government and some of the defendants. The suit was renumbered as title suit No. 59 of 1954 when it was transferred to the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal and thereafter on the creation of Potuakhali as District, the suit after transfer was registered as T.S. No. 146 of 1969. The suit was, however, withdrawn on 3.8.71 with permission to institute a fresh suit on the same cause of action. Title suit No. 3 of 1972 was there after filed on 24.1.1972 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Potuakhali inpursuance of the aforesaid permission. After amendment of Sections 86 and 87 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 an application for recording abatement of the suit was filed by the Government. The learned Sub-Judge by his order dated March, 24, 1973 recorded abatement of suit, which was affirmed by the High Court in revision. Against this order leave was granted to examine the question as to whether the Section 86 and 87 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by the Presidents Order Nos. 72, 135 and 137 of 1972 could be applied to the suit in respect of the lands in suit. This question was answered in the negative on taking the view that the suit was not hit by the amended provisions of Sections 86 and 87. It has been held that sub-section (3) will have operation only in respect of such accretions as have been contemplated in sub-section (3) of Section 87 of the Act. It has been further held that the provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3) of Section 86 of the Act cannot be given any retrospective effect beyond the date of coming into force of Part V of the Act in the area in which the diluviated land is situated.
